title: Introduce probabilistic capacity-budgeter and soft-preempt adapter for smoother decommits
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets see hard decommits during transient demand drops which causes bursty downstream latency and wasted warmup. This PR implements a probabilistic capacity budgeting component and a complementary soft-preempt adapter that together reduce hard preemptions while preserving long-run throughput guarantees.

Design summary: Introduces `capacity_budgeter` (service-level controller) which maintains a probabilistic budget for each pool using configurable percentile forecasts over recent usage windows and a small stochastic safety margin. Budgets are expressed as a fractional allocation of pool slots (0-1) and exposed as metrics for observability. The `soft_preempt_adapter` is a lightweight runtime-side shim that listens to budget revocations and converts immediate hard slot preempts into staged soft-preempt signals: runtime drains new allocations, migrates evictable requests, and issues a soft-fallback window before reclaiming.

Key behaviors: 1) Budgeter uses exponential-percentile smoothing: 95th/75th/50th windows fed into a weighted sampler to produce a target budget and a volatility score. 2) When budget deficit is signaled, soft_preempt_adapter attempts up to N grace cycles (configurable) before issuing a hard preempt; during grace gets a best-effort fallback routing. 3) Telemetry: new metrics `redwood.capacity_budget.pct`, `redwood.capacity_budget.volatility`, `redwood.soft_preempt.events`, and histograms for soft_grace_latency and fallback_routed_ratio. 4) Backpressure contract: controllers downstream may return CHOOSER_PREEMPT_SAFE to indicate they can accept soft preempt fallback. 5) Config: per-pool policy with min-reserve floor and a global conservative cap for safety.

Files touched (high-level): capacity_budgeter/ (controller, policy), runtime/soft_preempt_adapter/ (adapter + small API shim), telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new metric defs), e2e-tests/fleet_soft_preempt.integration (golden tests and simulated traffic), docs/ops/soft_preempt.md (operator guide), config/samples/pool_budget_policy.yaml.

Testing and QA: Unit tests cover budget calculations and volatility scoring; integration harness simulates spike→drop patterns and asserts soft_preempt events reduce hard preempt rate by >= 70% under test traffic. Added a cluster-level canary in staging for 48h before rollout. Load tests measured median tail latency improvement for cold reassigns (-18%) and a 22% reduction in overall evictions in the canary cluster.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy budgeter service in passive mode (metrics only) for 24h. 2) Enable advisory mode where soft_preempt_adapter only logs decisions. 3) Gradually enable soft_preempt with low concurrency pools (10% of fleet) for 72h. 4) Full rollout if evictions drop and SLOs stable. Feature gate: `prob_capacity_budgeter_v1` and `soft_preempt_v1`.

Backward compatibility: Existing controllers and pool configs remain unchanged; adapters default to conservative behavior. Operators can opt-out by setting min-reserve=1.

Open items and follow-ups: - Add per-tenant weighting into budgeter (ENG-2048). - Improve forecasting with short-term AR model (future PR). - Add dashboards and alerts for volatility spikes.

References: Linear ENG-1987, incident SUP-718, design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1987/probabilistic-capacity-budgeter (internal).

release_notes: Introduce probabilistic capacity budgeting and soft preempt adapter to reduce hard preemptions and evictions during transient demand drops. Add new telemetry and operator config. Rollout guarded by feature gates.
notes_for_ops: Feature gates: prob_capacity_budgeter_v1, soft_preempt_v1. Start in metrics-only mode. Recommended staging canary for 48h. Default conservative policy preserves existing behavior.
